extraction.note: Azure ships no Schedule K-1 model, and the generic layout read loses what a K-1's codes carry. Read by the declared custom model: the face and its attached statements, each coded figure under its box AND code, so a coded box reaches its route. The K-1 is its own section: its figures stay on this document (a K-1 is not a container). Declared the same way as k-1-1120s.

custom.reads: a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), Beneficiary's Share of Income, Deductions, Credits, etc., and the statements attached to it
instructions: Boxes 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 are coded: each figure in them prints beside a code letter (for example A, or AC). Give the box number in box and the letter or letters in code, exactly as printed. The other boxes print no code; leave code empty for them.

Where a coded box prints STMT, or an asterisk, instead of an amount, the figure is on an attached statement. Find that code's figure on the statement and report it under the same box and code, with the statement's page. Never report STMT or an asterisk as an amount.

For box 14 code I (Section 199A information), the statement is the QBI pass-through entity reporting. Report as box 14 code I each INCOME figure it prints for the beneficiary: ordinary business income (loss), rental income (loss), royalty income (loss), section 1231 gain (loss), other income (loss). Report its section 179 deduction, other deductions, W-2 wages, UBIA of qualified property and section 199A dividends in other_figures with their labels, never as box 14 code I.

Part II's lettered items say WHOSE K-1 this is — the partner, shareholder or beneficiary named on it, whether that person is an entity or a retirement plan, and who is responsible for reporting where they are a trust or a nominee. Read them as you read the numbered boxes: copy what is printed, and leave an item the page does not print out. They are not figures and they are not judgements; they are what says whether these figures belong on this return at all.
